description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
++ Major highlights and milestones of the implementation until December 2020:++
- The** redesign of the first part of the training resulted in a hybrid setting** (local venue and online trainers); this allowed to select 9 Trainers of Trainers (ToTs) (instead of 8), as the international travelling was reduced and the first part of the training was moved to hybrid online training. In case participants are not able to join the venue, they can also connect to the training from their home or office. The ToTs are 5 female and 4 male young professionals from different ministries (Ministry of Social Development, Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Physical Planning - Khartoum state) and SUDTT.
- Planning the first (hybrid) kick-off workshop in **collaboration with several ministries and local experts** in December 2020 – (the workshop happened on 13 January 2021 [https://www.itc.nl/news/2021/1/942418/successful-kick-off-workshop-for-ideamapsudan](https://www.itc.nl/news/2021/1/942418/successful-kick-off-workshop-for-ideamapsudan)).
- In **preparation of the first training package** (Oct-Dec. 2020), we concluded a) a training need assessment; b) the delineation of our focus area for Khartoum, c) selection of local pilot study areas; and d) first conceptualisation of locally relevant domains of deprivation. During the workshop, these preliminary assessments were discussed and adjusted according to the feedback of workshop participants. The invited participants of the workshop were policymakers, academia, NGOs and a representative of the Netherlands Embassy in Khartoum. Local participants were 26 and 15 online.
- **Development of online training materials** – all materials were developed for online training. Thus we moved the basic Geo-spatial training to complete online, which included also the preparation of a local training venue (for the hybrid training) where the ToTs would meet 1-2 mornings per week. The training was set up that trainers are connecting online.
​
In principle, the entire training is split into** 4 training packages (TP**) – the different TPs had to be adjusted to deal with the COVID-19 situation – overview of plans and adjustments:
o TP 1) is basic training of policy leaders, academia and representatives of NGOs on the relevance of spatial data to support urban deprivation analysis.
-> This was moved to several hybrid - online workshops (started in January 2021).
o TP 2) is the advanced technical training of young trainers (ToT) to co-create and sustain IDeAMapSudan. The ToT participants will become experts on Geo-information and Earth Observation and support the development of the operational IDeAMapSudan system - using spatial information for informed decision-making processes on urban development and to support the dialogue between local authorities and communities.
-> Until December 2020, the training was adjusted to have the basic training conducted as online training (with a local training venue)– with the plans to have later – more advance and interactive units as in-class training units (first in-person training was done September 2021 in Nairobi, Kenya: [https://twitter.com/MonikaKuffer/status/1439620705453322241](https://twitter.com/MonikaKuffer/status/1439620705453322241)).
o TP 3) is the training of different stakeholder groups (ranging from communities to policymakers) to use spatial data supported by IDeAMapSudan. The main lessons learned will be disseminated in form of best practice guides and used to frame TP4.
-> Plans had to be adapted to move to 2021 to have safe in-person training units.
o TP4) is the training and knowledge exchange to other parts of Sudan and across neighbouring countries to support peacebuilding in the Horn of Africa (South Sudan and Somalia) for scaling up the system beyond the implementation in Khartoum.
-> The will be done at a final stage (2022) of the TMT+ training.
​
++Overview of outputs in the log frame++
Output 1: 40 participants who are able to use IDeaMapSudan to support their work (incl. 9 ToT):
o Status December 2020: under development – not completed
o Until December 2020 – the selection of the 9 ToTs was almost completed – IDeaMapSudan is a co-design process that is ongoing throughout 2021.
Output 2: Training of Trainers programme with a total of 9 ToT, including 3 ToTs who will be an expert in software development and maintaining IDeaMapSudan.
o Status December 2020: under development – not completed
o Until December 2020 – the selection process of the 9 ToTs was almost completed (ToTs training started in 2021)
Output 3: IDeaMapSudan, a spatial information system for mapping deprived areas including an open access database
o Status December 2020: under development – not completed
o The completed components until December 2020: Stakeholder mapping and defining the extent of the study area.
Output 4: A plugin for the QGIS software (open free software)
o Status December 2020: not completed
o Planned for 2021
Output 5: A mobile app that supports field data collection
o Status December 2020: not completed
o The first pre-selection of suitable apps was done as part of the training curriculum.
Output 6: Approximately 200 people (2 different communities will gain awareness on spatial information related to risks and opportunities (e.g., livelihood)
o Status December 2020: not completed
o Planned for 2021
Output 7: Best practices on peace building between states, regional and local authorities and societies at large will help to effectively prevent and resolve conflict in a nonviolent and inclusive manner
o Status December 2020: not completed
o Planned for 2022
